note: Adapted from Silvestri 1914; the original is in Latin (Contribuzione alla conoscenza dei Termitidi e Termitofili dell'Africa occidentale. I. Termitidi, Bollettino del Laboratorio di Zoologia Generale e Agraria della R. Scuola Superiore d'Agricoltura in Portici 9). Type locality: Kindia, Guinea. Biology: the species builds a subconical nest of humus soil on the ground, about 20 cm high and with a base of about the same diameter; the author found three true queens and one king in the royal cell of one nest; the soldiers jump by snapping their mandibles (as the author recorded for Neocapritermes), at about one soldier per hundred workers. The original uses a comma as the decimal mark (e.g. 2,86 for 2.86 mm); this has been converted to a decimal point here. Pl. LXXXII figs. 1—4 (queen head and pronotum in front and lateral view, soldier head in front and lateral view) are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Very close to Pericapritermes urgens, differing in the alate (queen) being slightly larger, antennal segment 3 slightly longer, the shape of the meso- and metanotum, and the soldier being slightly larger.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Queen (Regina): body yellowish brown, chestnut; head nearly chestnut; clypeus yellowish brown, rust-coloured; meso- and metanotum partly yellowish white; sternites 1—5 yellowish white except for their pale yellowish brown sides; membranous parts dirty cream; pleurites with red spots; legs red rust-coloured. Head (Pl. LXXXII, 1—2): the clypeus slightly swollen, the fontanelle window (fenestra) elongate-oval and yellowish white; compound eyes large and distinctly projecting; the distance between the ocellus and the compound eye less than the long diameter of the ocellus; antennae incomplete, segment 2 slightly longer than segment 3, segments 3—5 nearly equal in length. The posterior margin of the pronotum is almost without a concavity; meso- and metanotum slightly narrowing posteriorly, their posterior margin broadly and shallowly incised, the posterior corners pointed. Measurements (mm): body length 25, abdomen width 5; head length 1.04, head width 0.91; long diameter of the compound eye 0.39; hind tibia 1.34.

sections.label: Nymph
sections.text: Body straw-yellow, compound eyes turning black, antennae 15-segmented, segment 2 slightly longer than segment 3. Measurements (mm): body length 7, wing-pad length 2.8.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Large soldier: body yellowish white, head ochre, more or less rust-tinged in front, mandibles black. Head (Pl. LXXXII, 3—4) twice as long as wide, of the typical shape; antennae 14-segmented, segment 4 shorter than segment 3, segment 5 slightly longer than segment 4. The posterior margin of the anterior lobe of the pronotum is slightly concave in the middle and bears a few long hairs; the posterior margins of the pronotum, mesonotum and metanotum each bear several long hairs. The coxa of the first pair of legs has 2—3 short hairs on its outer margin, and the inner margin of the tibia has a few weak hairs. Abdominal tergites with very minute hairs, rather many short hairs and several long hairs (especially posteriorly); sternites with very minute hairs, short hairs and long hairs posteriorly. Measurements (mm): body length 6.5; head length 2.86, head width 1.39; left mandible length 1.72; antennal length 2.40; hind tibia 1.32. Small soldier: antennae 14-segmented, segment 3 nearly equal to segment 2 and longer than segment 4. Measurements (mm): body length 5.8; head length 2.54, head width 1.28; left mandible length 1.64; antennal length 2.10; hind tibia 1.15. The remaining soldiers are intermediate in size.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Body cream-coloured, head ochre-yellow to yellowish white, the abdomen greyish from the food it contains. The clypeus of the head is slightly swollen; antennae 14-segmented, segment 2 about 1/4 longer than segment 3, segment 3 about twice as long as segment 4, segment 5 about 1/4 longer than segment 4. The posterior margin of the anterior lobe of the pronotum is not, or hardly, concave in the middle. Leg hairs well developed: the outer side of the coxa of the first pair of legs with 2 short, rather stout hairs, the hairs of the tibia finer than in the preceding species. Abdominal tergites and sternites with shorter hairs, short hairs and several rather long hairs posteriorly. Measurements (mm): body length 4; head length 0.97, head width 1.04; antennal length 1.35; hind tibia 0.92.
